static_traits.name: Han Wei
static_traits.family_status: Living alone; other family members not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Avoids social interaction with students and colleagues; interaction decreases
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, relatively good logic, high cooperation; able to identify and describe anxiety and self-doubt; tends to use self-deprecating labels (such as 'old fool'); attention biased toward negative cues and tends to ignore positive feedback

basic_info.main_problem: I believe students judge me as incompetent and old based on how they look at me in class, which makes me feel anxious and insecure in every class.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings are affecting my confidence and performance in the classroom; I want to find ways to be more confident in teaching.
growth_experiences: A few months ago, a student's comment about age triggered a sense of being judged; afterward in class, students' whispering and laughter intensified this feeling, gradually developing into anxiety and self-doubt at every teaching session, and the client began avoiding interaction with students and colleagues; sleep and eating were also affected.

core_beliefs: Age means I have no value and will be looked down on by students

special_situations.event: A student once commented on his age in class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If someone mentions my age, it means that because of my age I am not suited to teaching and not competent enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles efforts to change teaching methods to prove ability; reflects on the self after class and avoids informal interaction with students
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I am old and incompetent, I am an 'old fool'.

special_situations.event: During class, students whisper or laugh
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If students speak in low voices or laugh, they must be talking about me and thinking I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pays excessive attention to students' expressions and subtle reactions, constantly adjusting teaching pace and content in class; reduces question-and-answer interaction to avoid being negated in public
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are mocking me and looking down on me.

special_situations.event: Students appear distracted or uninterested in class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If students get distracted, it means I lecture very poorly, caused by my insufficient ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids eye contact with students and reduces communication with colleagues to lower the chances of being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just too bad; no one wants to listen to me.

special_situations.event: Students actively asking questions, participating, or giving positive feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive reactions are not reliable, if I accept them I will appear to be deceiving myself
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses doubt and explanations to negate positive signals (such as 'they were just being polite') in order to maintain a consistent self-view
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; they do not really recognize me.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and respected by students, proving one's professional value and competence
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being laughed at, belittled and rejected, worrying about appearing incompetent and losing face
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of negative evaluation by maintaining detachment and avoiding interaction
Controlling possible humiliation through excessive self-monitoring and constantly adjusting teaching
Negating positive feedback to avoid the unease of having one's self-schema challenged

object_relations.self_representation: A teacher who is easily judged, vulnerable, and possibly incompetent
object_relations.object_representation: A student body that is picky, contemptuous, and liable to mock oneself at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When students whisper, laugh, or appear distracted in class
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes the other person views them with contempt and negation (transferentially projecting inner self-deprecation onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In an affirmative and resolute tone, asserts 'they are just laughing at me / looking down on me', gives the other party no space to clarify, and avoids further interaction.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others point out students' positive feedback, or invite them to consider other explanations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing that acknowledging positive evidence is equated with self-deception or that negated feelings are not understood
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Negates positive evidence with reasons such as 'they were just being polite / going through the motions', in a calm but resolute tone, repeatedly returning to negative explanations.

manifestations: Lives alone; recently avoids social contact with students and colleagues
Feels isolated and judged in the classroom, finding it hard to build genuine connections with others
outcomes: Declining self-confidence and performance at work

manifestations: Highly sensitive to others' gazes and evaluations, experiencing being constrained by external expectations
To avoid being evaluated, reducing interaction, action choices are limited by fear
outcomes: Persistent self-monitoring and tension; difficulty expressing oneself genuinely and making contact

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Attributing experiences of self-doubt and shame to students' contempt and mockery
Automatically assuming others' negative thoughts in class without verification

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Constantly doubting oneself in class and closely watching others' reactions
Reduces interaction and holds back in tone to avoid mistakes, finding it hard to teach and communicate spontaneously

exception_events.target_problem: In class, when encountering students snickering, whispering, or being distracted, the client usually interprets it as a negation of their ability and age, thereby feeling anxious and avoiding interaction.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In one class, some students actively asked questions and participated in discussion, and someone gave positive feedback; classroom interaction went more smoothly than before.
exception_events.reason: Clues: took different approaches (tried changing teaching style and increasing interaction with students); situationally, students were more interested in that day's topic, resulting in higher participation and positive feedback.

positive_force: Having a stable teaching position and professional background
Willing to seek help and actively cooperate in practicing cognitive restructuring
In class there indeed is evidence of students actively participating and giving positive feedback
Has proactively tried adjusting teaching style and increasing interaction
Has a close friend who can be relied on (potential support)
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as mind reading, overgeneralization and negating positive feedback are significant
Self-deprecating labeling thinking reinforces the sense of incompetence
Social avoidance and excessive self-monitoring maintain the anxiety cycle
Negative selective attention to external cues (biased toward snickering/whispering etc.)
Anxiety affects sleep and eating, further weakening work performance and confidence

target_behavior.behavior: Significant anxiety and self-deprecation in class, and avoiding interaction with students
antecedent: Recalling the earlier comments about age
target_behavior.core_reason: Interprets students' neutral / ambiguous behavior as a negation of their own ability and age, reinforcing the core belief 'I am incompetent' (mind reading and overgeneralization)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the subjective risk of being evaluated or publicly humiliated, to gain a short-term sense of safety
target_behavior.consequence: Teaching performance declines and self-confidence is damaged; relationships with students and colleagues become distant; sleep and eating are affected

target_behavior.behavior: Disqualifies or ignores students' positive feedback and engagement signals
antecedent: In class, students actively ask questions or participate
target_behavior.core_reason: Excludes inconsistent information to maintain the negative self-schema, avoiding the unease brought by cognitive dissonance
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a stable, predictable self-narrative to reduce feelings of uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty consolidating successful experiences; negative beliefs are continuously reinforced and anxiety persists undiminished
